title: Affine sections of recursive powers of an arbitrary quasi-coherent ideal module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $K$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $i:K\to\mathcal O_X$ a morphism [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(P_n,j_n)$ be its recursive image powers [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. For every $n\geq0$, $P_n$ is quasi-coherent and, on every affine open $V$, $\operatorname{im}(j_n(V))=\operatorname{im}(i(V))^n$ as ideals of $\mathcal O_X(V)$. No monicity or finite-type hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Lemma 01PQ (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open), affine ideal powers; proof of the existing private lemma AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.powers_affine_sections, Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/CoherentSupportVanishingIdealNilpotence.lean, lines 108-154.

proof.text: For n=0 the power is the unit and its section ideal is R; for n=1 it is K and its section ideal is the image of i. For each subsequent power, the tensor product is quasi-coherent and its image is quasi-coherent.

On an affine open the tensor-section map is bijective, and applying the image-section formula to the multiplication map identifies its range with J times the module of sections of the previous power. Composing with its inclusion into R gives J times J^(n+1)=J^(n+2). This is the proved private helper powers_affine_sections in the recorded source module; the new GeneralIdealPowerAffineSections module exposes this already proved fact as a public theorem, importing the helper through import all; it does not reprove the support-nilpotence theorem.

theorem general_ideal_power_affine_sections {X : Scheme.{u}} {I : X.Modules}
    (ι : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) [I.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∀ n : ℕ, (idealSheafPower ι n).1.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ∀ V : X.affineOpens,
        (LinearMap.range ((idealSheafPower ι n).2.val.app (op V.1)).hom :
          Ideal Γ(X, V.1)) =
          (LinearMap.range (ι.val.app (op V.1)).hom : Ideal Γ(X, V.1)) ^ n
